result.response:
I have resolved the issue in [compiler.py](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-lc4renhj/django/db/models/sql/compiler.py).

### Root Cause
When fast-deleting an unfiltered queryset (e.g. `Model.objects.all().delete()`), `self.query.alias_map` is empty because the initial alias for the base table hasn't been initialized yet. Consequently, [`SQLDeleteCompiler.single_alias`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-lc4renhj/django/db/models/sql/compiler.py#L1408-L1412) evaluated `sum(...) == 1` to `0 == 1` (`False`), causing [`SQLDeleteCompiler.as_sql()`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-lc4renhj/django/db/models/sql/compiler.py#L1423-L1440) to fall back to the multi-table subquery deletion path (`DELETE FROM table WHERE id IN (SELECT id FROM table)`).

### Fix
Call `self.query.get_initial_alias()` in [`SQLDeleteCompiler.single_alias`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-lc4renhj/django/db/models/sql/compiler.py#L1408-L1412) to ensure the base table is present in `alias_map` and `alias_refcount` before counting active aliases.
